decisions.question: How often should another faction's truck pop its smoke dischargers?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.319.0 (row 573): raiders' trucks carry no chemfuel to reload, so a truck of theirs comes loaded for one salvo and pops it the first time it is hit while you are a threat.

options.label: Once a visit
options.detail: As built: one salvo each time it comes to a map

options.label: Every hit, 10 s apart
options.detail: Loaded free each time, as often as yours with the switch on

decisions.why: A real truck carries a few reloads at most; smoke every 10 seconds would blind your guns for the whole fight

decisions.question: Without Combat Extended our ring guns feed from steel. Should steel count as rounds in the ammunition locker?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.319.0 (row 574): a round is whatever a fitted gun's ammunition allows, as Vehicle Framework itself decides, so a gun truck's steel (and the dischargers' chemfuel) goes in the locker.

options.label: Yes, as built
options.detail: Whatever the truck's guns fire counts as rounds

options.label: No, never raw materials
options.detail: Steel and chemfuel stay ordinary cargo; the locker holds only real ammunition items

decisions.why: It is what those guns actually load; without Combat Extended there are no ammunition items, so 'no' would leave the locker empty

decisions.question: Should the turbocharger fitting be refused on an engine that is already turbocharged as built?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.320.0 (row 576): a built-in turbo is now a part like a fitted one. The fitting is still offered on those engines and adds its x1.2 on top; if the one turbo part fails, both power losses apply (about 0.58 of rated).

options.label: Refuse it there
options.detail: The Fittings window says the engine already has a turbocharger; any already fitted stays until taken off

options.label: Allow it, as now
options.detail: Read as a bigger turbo on top of the built-in one, with the double loss when it fails

decisions.why: One turbo part stands for one turbo; a second fitting on it has no physical meaning and makes the failure harsher than either alone

decisions.question: When should people take a preventive (penoxycyline, a vaccine) by rule?
decisions.context: Built in Medical 0.28.0 (row 591): they take it while someone in the colony has the disease. But in the game, and in your mods as read on 26 Nov 2026, no disease passes between people, so that protects against the next strike, not the one under way.

options.label: While someone has it
options.detail: As built: it reacts to a strike, and guards against a second one while the first runs

options.label: Always, where the biome brings it
options.detail: Standing protection, as a drug policy's schedule already gives; uses stock steadily, held by the reserve

options.label: A setting for either
options.detail: One more choice on the Emergency dosing page

decisions.why: Standing protection is what a drug policy's schedule already does in the game, so a second way to do it adds little; reacting to a strike is the part the game lacks

decisions.question: A drug policy has no tick for a plain medicine, only a schedule. What should let someone take a preventive on their own?
decisions.context: Built in Medical 0.28.0 (row 591): your card said people take their own 'by their drug policy', but a policy can only allow a drug for joy or for an addiction. As built, the policy decides for anything addictive or taken for pleasure; a plain medicine is taken whenever the need is set to doctors and self.

options.label: The need's own setting
options.detail: As built: a plain medicine needs no policy line

options.label: Only if scheduled in the policy
options.detail: Strictest: nobody takes one unless you have scheduled that drug for them

options.label: Doctors give it to everyone
options.detail: Nobody takes their own; a doctor walks to each person, on their feet or not

decisions.why: With 'scheduled only' almost nobody would ever take one, since the game already doses a scheduled drug by itself; a doctors' round costs your doctors hours in an outbreak

decisions.question: A medicine worth 300 silver or more is kept for saving a life. Is 300 the right mark for medicines?
decisions.context: Built in Medical 0.28.0, from your card of 26 Nov 2026, with triage's mark for a rare tool. I was wrong on the card to name Hydra: it is worth 64. Among the medicines whose Def states a value, none reaches 300 (regeneration serum 150, Tyrox 105), so the rule may match nothing in your game today.

options.label: Keep 300
options.detail: One mark for rare tools and rare medicines; it catches glitterworld items a mod may add

options.label: Lower it to 100
options.detail: Tyrox and the regeneration serum would be kept for life-threatening needs only

options.label: No mark
options.detail: Cost never holds a medicine back

decisions.why: A cheap medicine held back does more harm than a dear one used; 300 keeps the rule for the truly rare without second-guessing ordinary stock
